newsitem.title: USA: EU to pursue WTO case against US Helms-Burton law.
newsitem.headline: EU to pursue WTO case against US Helms-Burton law.

text.p: The European Union will press ahead with its complaint against the United States in the World Trade Organization over Washington's anti-Cuba trade law, a senior official said on Tuesday.

"We shall proceed with our complaint to the WTO until the issues are resolved," European Commission Vice President Leon Brittan told reporters after he and Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo met with U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright.

The Helms-Burton act, named after its congressional sponsors, allows, among other things, Americans to sue foreign firms or individuals deemed to have profited from investments in property confiscated by Cuba's communist government.
President Clinton has twice suspended that provision for six months -- the last time on January 3 -- but Brittan made clear that Europe does not believe that went far enough.
"I hope we will be able to resolve the issue," he said. But he did not provide any details of any possible compromise between the two sides.
